rules: n >= 1: number + suffix; suffix is 'st' when n%10==1, 'nd' when n%10==2, 'rd' when n%10==3, else 'th' (1->1st, 2->2nd, 3->3rd, 4->4th, 21->21st, 22->22nd, 101->101st).
Teens exception: if n%100 is in 11..13 the suffix is 'th' regardless of the last digit (11->11th, 12->12th, 13->13th, 111->111th, 112->112th, 213->213th).

injection_strategy: tbx.go is a bespoke, repo-local stdlib extension (package core, registered as stdlib.Values['tbx']). The defect.patch introduces the whole file already carrying three independent faults across separate helpers/branches; the accepted_solution.patch repairs all three.

bugs.fault: case 3 returns "th" instead of "rd", so any value whose last digit is 3 (outside the teens) gets the wrong ending: 3->3th, 23->23th, 103->103th.

Teens are detected with `n == 11 || n == 12 || n == 13` instead of `n%100` in 11..13, so teens above one hundred escape the exception: 111->111st, 112->112nd (113 happens to read correctly only because of BUG1's case-3 change).
Negative inputs drop the leading minus sign: -1->1st, -22->22nd, -111->111st.

partial_fix_traps: The prompt only gestures at 'wrong ending' and shows 1st/2nd/3rd, which points at BUG1 (the last-digit suffix) and nothing else. Fixing only case 3 -> 'rd' still leaves the teens-above-100 checks (one_eleven, one_twelve) and the negative checks (minus_one, minus_twenty_two) failing.
Fixing BUG1 and BUG2 but not BUG3 leaves both negative checks failing.
Zero is a control: the broken code already prints 0th, so a fix that only special-cases zero changes nothing observable.
expected_failure_summary: 12 hidden checks. Broken passes the 5 controls only (one, two, five, twenty_one, zero) -> 5/12 = 0.417, well under the 0.9 gate. Accepted (all three bugs repaired) passes 12/12 = 1.000. Fixing only the hinted BUG1 raises broken to 8/12 = 0.667, still under 0.9.
